budget_items.topic: ADU sewer tie-in fee, existing regulation
budget_items.what_was_said: The current regulation already charges a fee for a third connection or bedroom before any new ADU-specific language is added.
A proposed fee to tie in an ADU and a separate proposed fee per bedroom were discussed, based on flow volume rather than distance.

budget_items.topic: ADU minimum square footage vs. house minimum connection size
budget_items.what_was_said: State law sets a minimum ADU size while the town's regulation sets a higher minimum for a regular house connection.

budget_items.topic: Sewer tie-in fees vs. reserve/reverse capacity fee
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner asked how ADU connection money would be allocated among different existing fee categories (tie-in fees versus a reserve capacity fee), since the funds are split among different accounts; no figure was resolved.

budget_items.topic: Proposed flat ADU fee if tying into the house
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner suggested that if an ADU ties into the existing house line rather than the street, the fee could be a flat amount rather than the full new-connection fee.

The business manager explained a resident's water usage figure had been revised upward by the water department after a meter change, inflating her sewer bill; he proposed crediting her account on the next bill.

decisions.decision: Commissioners agreed to consolidate Dan's and Andrew's separate ADU fee ideas into one draft document to discuss at the next meeting before bringing it to town council.
Proposed (not yet voted) that an ADU sewer line must tie into the existing sewer line on the property, with no new connections directly from the street.
Discussed that if a direct connection to the street line were ever unavoidable, it would be charged the same as a full new house connection fee rather than a lesser ADU fee.
Each commissioner agreed to take a copy of the draft ADU proposal home to review before refining it further at a future meeting.

minutes.headline: Sewer Commission drafted proposed ADU sewer connection fees and tie-in rules but took no final vote on them.
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission spent most of the meeting workshopping a proposed regulation and fee structure for Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) sewer connections, comparing draft language from a commissioner and from staff, and discussing tie-in methods, easements, metering, and billing scenarios without taking a formal vote on the policy. The commission also voted to approve prior minutes, voted to credit a resident's sewer bill after a water-meter-driven billing error, and previewed upcoming agenda items including two easement waiver requests and a flow-increase vote for a change of use.

what_happened.line: Commission drafted ADU sewer connection fees and tie-in rules but took no final vote, planning one consolidated draft before town council.
Commission voted to credit a resident's sewer bill after a water-meter change had inflated her usage reading.
Draft rule discussed: an ADU line must tie into the existing house line, not connect directly to the street, or pay a full new-connection fee.
Commission previewed two upcoming easement waiver requests and a flow-increase vote for a retail space becoming a gym.

why_it_matters: Anyone adding an accessory dwelling unit will owe a sewer connection fee that is still being drafted, not yet set or voted.
A water-meter change can move a sewer bill on its own, as this credit shows, without any error by the resident.
The change-of-use flow vote and easement waivers ahead touch how much sewer capacity other properties can claim.
